segments.speaker: me
segments.text: Afternoon. We have the redlined master services agreement back from the retailer. Let's go clause by clause.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Most of the changes are cosmetic. The big ones are indemnity, liability cap, and data processing.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: They want twelve months of fees as the cap, but uncapped for data breaches.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Counsel's view is that we should never accept uncapped breach liability. Her advice is to counter with a super-cap at three times annual fees, and if they push, we can go to five but only if they drop the consequential damages carve-out. She also said our cyber policy won't cover contractual liability above the cap, so anything we agree to beyond it is effectively uninsured.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: And she flagged that the indemnity language would make us liable for their own misuse of the API, which she thinks is unenforceable in English courts anyway, but we shouldn't rely on that.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: They attached their own DPA instead of ours. It's longer but mostly equivalent.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Mostly. The sub-processor notification period is fourteen days in theirs and thirty in ours. Ops says fourteen is workable.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Net sixty instead of net thirty.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: Finance won't love it but it's a big account. Let's accept net forty-five as a counter.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: I'll update the redline and send it back by Thursday.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Just the governing law clause, they want England, which is fine for us.

planted.quote: Counsel's view is that we should never accept uncapped breach liability
